statement: Prolonged denervation degrades the distal nerve's capacity to support regeneration — Schwann cells lose their growth-supportive state — and this decline, alongside muscle atrophy, is a principal reason that proximal nerve injuries recover poorly.

context.model: chronic denervation after proximal nerve injury

measurement.endpoint: Schwann cell support and reinnervation capacity over time
measurement.effect: progressive loss of support with time since denervation

replication.note: Review-level synthesis; the primary evidence is largely rodent.

limitations: human evidence is inferential, from outcome-versus-delay data rather than from tissue

provenance.method: manual reasoning from the cited sources' abstracts (Crossref/Europe PMC), checked 2026-09-14; no source opened at figure level
